subject.title: [Bug]: `openclaw models auth login` on node host writes OAuth token locally instead of syncing to gateway

question: Should `models auth login` on a configured remote node host fail closed with gateway-host instructions, or should OpenClaw add a secure gateway-forwarded auth sync path?
rationale: The bug is clear, but the durable fix chooses where OAuth credentials may be created, stored, and transferred across the node/gateway boundary.

options.title: Fail closed before OAuth starts
options.body: Block remote node-host OAuth login with a clear instruction to run auth on the gateway host, preventing local token consumption without adding credential transfer.

options.title: Design gateway-owned auth forwarding
options.body: Allow node-host login only after adding an authenticated gateway credential-transfer protocol with security review and upgrade tests.

options.title: Document the current limitation
options.body: Leave runtime behavior unchanged and document that remote node users must run OAuth login on the gateway, accepting continued risk of silent local writes.

recommendation.title: Fail closed before OAuth starts
recommendation.body: Block remote node-host OAuth login with a clear instruction to run auth on the gateway host, preventing local token consumption without adding credential transfer.

likelyOwner.reason: Vincent Koc authored the recent member-side exact-fix attempt and is the clearest available owner for the security-sensitive fix-shape decision among the related history.
